nitrite and nitrate reducers were highly affected in the cathode and displayed a high diversity.
the microbial fuel cell is a promising tool for denitrification, and that the denitrifying bacterial community is a key player to control the process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of nitrite as an electron acceptors in MFCs may be a promising approach for nitrogen removal, but may result in significant accumulation of N2O.
nitrate reduction is more effective in removing nitrogen than the reduction of nitrite, but it is also more efficient in terms of current production.

the use of nitrite as electron acceptor in the MFC cathode is not a suitable strategy to reduce N2O emissions in the cathode and that the use of denitrification as an electron sink should be carefully evaluated in MFCs.
